findings.title: Clamp removed: extracted files show over 100% progress and lose their 'Done' and success states
findings.problem: This change undoes the earlier fix. The diff removes `Math.min(100, ...)` and the comment explaining why it was there. Extracted archives have local_size > remote_size, so percentDownloaded now goes above 100 (local 20, remote 10 gives 200; 199 is also possible). The consumer src/angular/src/app/pages/files/transfer-row.component.html line 28 prints the raw value as text ("200%"). The bar width at line 35 is clamped separately, so the bar still looks right. Two checks use strict `=== 100` and now silently fail for these files: line 33 drops the `progress-fill--success` class, and line 53 drops the 'Done' ETA label and shows '-' instead. The existing unit test view-file.service.spec.ts:245-247 expects [20,10,100] and [100,50,100] to clamp to 100, so it will now fail.
findings.fix_hint: restore Math.min(100, Math.trunc(100.0 * localSize / remoteSize)) and its explanatory comment
findings.why_it_matters: Users see impossible values like '199%'. Finished extracted downloads lose the success styling and the 'Done' label. The unit test suite also fails.

members.title: Removed clamp lets percentDownloaded exceed 100 for extracted files
members.problem: The diff deletes both the `Math.min(100, ...)` clamp and the comment explaining it was there precisely because extracted archives have `local_size` (unpacked) greater than `remote_size` (compressed), which otherwise yields percentages like 199%. Removing it reinstates that exact bug.
members.why_it_matters: transfer-row.component.html only clamps the progress-bar width defensively; the percentage text, the `progress-fill--success` class, and the 'Done' label are all gated on the raw, unclamped value (`=== 100`), so extracted files will show '199%'/'200%' and never get the success styling or 'Done' state. This also breaks the existing unit test (view-file.service.spec.ts ~line 237-248) which explicitly asserts local>remote cases clamp to 100.
members.fix_hint: Restore `Math.min(100, Math.trunc(100.0 * localSize / remoteSize))` (and ideally the removed comment) in the ternary.

members.title: Extracted files show over-100% progress and lose completion indicators
members.problem: For local_size=20 and remote_size=10, the changed expression returns 200 instead of 100. The existing regression vectors in view-file.service.spec.ts explicitly require 100 for this case. transfer-row.component.html displays the raw percentage at line 28 and requires exactly 100 for success styling (line 33) and the 'Done' label (line 53). Its width clamp at line 35 protects only bar geometry: completed extracted files now display 200% and lose both completion indicators.

members.fix_hint: Restore Math.min(100, ...) around the calculated percentage and retain the existing extracted-file regression vectors.

members.title: Removing the 100% clamp brings back the >100% progress bug for extracted files, so their row also loses its 'Done' state and success styling
members.problem: The diff removes the Math.min(100, ...) clamp. The deleted comment says it was there for one case: extracted files, where the unpacked local size is larger than the remote archive. With the clamp gone, localSize=20 and remoteSize=10 give percentDownloaded=200. Three places in transfer-row.component.html read this value. Line 28 shows the raw number, so the user sees '200%'. Line 33 checks `=== 100` for the success class, which is now false. Line 53 checks `=== 100` to show 'Done' in the ETA column, which is now false, so the column shows '-' instead. Only the bar width at line 35 stays correct, because the template clamps it on its own. The unit test at view-file.service.spec.ts:245-247 still expects vectors [20,10,100] and [100,50,100], so this diff will fail the existing test suite.
members.why_it_matters: Every user who downloads archives that get auto-extracted would see a nonsense progress percentage, and finished items would no longer show 'Done' or the success styling. The existing unit test fails, which blocks CI.
members.fix_hint: Restore Math.min(100, ...) (and its comment), or if the clamp is meant to move, make every `=== 100` consumer in transfer-row.component.html use `>= 100` and clamp the displayed text

members.title: Removing the clamp moves the 0-100 range rule out of the view-model and onto its consumers, and only one of them enforces it
members.problem: ViewFileService is the layer that turns ModelFile into ViewFile, and before this diff it was the one place that kept `percentDownloaded` between 0 and 100. With the clamp gone, every consumer has to handle values above 100 itself. The only consumer, transfer-row.component.html, does so for one binding: the bar width on line 35. The text on line 28 and the `=== 100` checks on lines 33 and 53 assume the value is already in range. An extracted file (local size larger than remote) will show something like "199%". Its success styling and the `=== 100` branch also stop matching, so it no longer looks complete.
members.why_it_matters: Users will see a progress value over 100% and completed extracted files will lose their 'done' styling. A range rule that each consumer must repeat will drift, and it already has here: one binding clamps while three do not.
members.fix_hint: restore Math.min(100, ...) in the service so ViewFile.percentDownloaded stays a normalized 0-100 value; the template's width clamp can stay as a defensive fallback

findings.title: The diff goes against the documented contract in the existing spec, which still requires the clamp
findings.problem: The service spec states the intended behavior: `// Extracted files: local (unpacked) > remote (archive) clamps at 100, not 199%`, with vectors `[20, 10, 100]` and `[100, 50, 100]`. The diff removes the clamp but leaves the spec unchanged, so these vectors will now produce 200 instead of 100 and the test will fail. Nothing in the diff explains the change in behavior.
findings.fix_hint: either revert the clamp removal, or, if the change is intentional, update the spec vectors and every percentDownloaded consumer in transfer-row.component.html together
findings.why_it_matters: This looks like an accidental regression of a fix made on purpose, not a deliberate design change. Either way, the service contract and its tests now disagree.
